text: And it happened to us just as he had interpreted: I was restored to my position, and the other man was hanged.

speaker: pharaoh
name: Pharaoh
text: I had a dream, and no one can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.

speaker: joseph
name: Joseph
text: I myself cannot do it,

speaker: joseph
text: but God will give Pharaoh a sound answer.

speaker: pharaoh
text: In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile,

speaker: pharaoh
text: when seven cows, well-fed and sleek, came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.

speaker: pharaoh
text: After them, seven other cows—sickly, ugly, and thin—came up. I have never seen such ugly cows in all the land of Egypt!

speaker: pharaoh
text: Then the thin, ugly cows devoured the seven well-fed cows that were there first.

speaker: pharaoh
text: When they had devoured them, however, no one could tell that they had done so; their appearance was as ugly as it had been before. Then I awoke.

speaker: pharaoh
text: In my dream I also saw seven heads of grain, plump and ripe, growing on a single stalk.

speaker: pharaoh
text: After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted—withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind.

speaker: pharaoh
text: And the thin heads of grain swallowed the seven plump ones. I told this dream to the magicians, but no one could explain it to me.

speaker: joseph
text: The dreams of Pharaoh are one and the same. God has revealed to Pharaoh what He is about to do.

text: Cursed be their anger, for it is strong, and their wrath, for it is cruel! I will disperse them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.

speaker: jacob
text: Judah, your brothers shall praise you. Your hand shall be on the necks of your enemies; your father’s sons shall bow down to you.

speaker: jacob
text: Judah is a young lion— my son, you return from the prey. Like a lion he crouches and lies down; like a lioness, who dares to rouse him?

speaker: jacob
text: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.

speaker: jacob
text: He ties his donkey to the vine, his colt to the choicest branch. He washes his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.

speaker: jacob
text: His eyes are darker than wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.

speaker: jacob
text: Zebulun shall dwell by the seashore and become a harbor for ships; his border shall extend to Sidon.

speaker: jacob
text: Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the sheepfolds.

speaker: jacob
text: He saw that his resting place was good and that his land was pleasant, so he bent his shoulder to the burden and submitted to labor as a servant.

speaker: jacob
text: Dan shall provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel.

speaker: jacob
text: He will be a snake by the road, a viper in the path that bites the horse’s heels so that its rider tumbles backward.

speaker: jacob
text: I await Your salvation, O LORD.

speaker: jacob
text: Gad will be attacked by raiders, but he will attack their heels.

speaker: jacob
text: Asher’s food will be rich; he shall provide royal delicacies.

speaker: jacob
text: Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns.

speaker: jacob
text: Joseph is a fruitful vine— a fruitful vine by a spring, whose branches scale the wall.

speaker: jacob
text: The archers attacked him with bitterness; they aimed at him in hostility.

speaker: jacob
text: Yet he steadied his bow, and his strong arms were tempered by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, in the name of the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel,

speaker: jacob
text: by the God of your father who helps you, and by the Almighty who blesses you, with blessings of the heavens above, with blessings of the depths below, with blessings of the breasts and womb.

speaker: jacob
text: The blessings of your father have surpassed the blessings of the ancient mountains and the bounty of the everlasting hills. May they rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince of his brothers.

speaker: jacob
text: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the plunder.

speaker: jacob
text: I am about to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite.

speaker: jacob
text: The cave is in the field of Machpelah near Mamre, in the land of Canaan. This is the field Abraham purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.

speaker: jacob
text: There Abraham and his wife Sarah are buried, there Isaac and his wife Rebekah are buried, and there I buried Leah.

speaker: jacob
text: The field and the cave that is in it were purchased from the Hittites.

speaker: joseph
name: Joseph
text: If I have found favor in your eyes, please tell Pharaoh that

speaker: joseph
text: my father made me swear an oath when he said, ‘I am about to die. You must bury me in the tomb that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.’ Now let me go and bury my father, and then return.

speaker: jacob
name: Jacob (Israel)
text: I am about to die. You must bury me in the tomb that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.

speaker: pharaoh
name: Pharaoh
text: Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear to do.

speaker: canaanites
name: The Canaanites
text: This is a solemn ceremony of mourning by the Egyptians.

speaker: josephs-brothers
name: Joseph’s brothers
text: What if Joseph bears a grudge? Then he will surely repay us for all the evil that we did to him.

speaker: josephs-brothers
text: Before he died, your father commanded,

speaker: josephs-brothers
text: ‘This is what you are to say to Joseph: I beg you, please forgive the transgression and sin of your brothers, for they did you wrong.’ So now, Joseph, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.

speaker: jacob
text: This is what you are to say to Joseph: I beg you, please forgive the transgression and sin of your brothers, for they did you wrong.

speaker: josephs-brothers
text: We are your slaves!

speaker: joseph
text: Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?

speaker: joseph
text: As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good, in order to accomplish a day like this—to preserve the lives of many people.

speaker: joseph
text: Therefore do not be afraid. I will provide for you and your little ones.

speaker: joseph
text: I am about to die, but God will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land He promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

speaker: joseph
text: God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.
